evals.name: account-withdrawal-behavior-tests
evals.prompt: Add tests for Account::withdraw in tests/AccountTest.php. It should allow withdrawing the available balance, reject one dollar beyond the balance, and keep the original balance when the withdrawal is rejected. Use the existing Pest style.
evals.expected_output: Writes readable Pest tests with behavior-shaped names, concrete Money values, visible Arrange / Act / Assert shape, and specific assertions for result and balance state.

assertions.text: Names tests after withdrawal behavior and outcome
Uses concrete boundary values for exact balance and beyond balance
Asserts both rejection reason and unchanged balance for the failure case

evals.name: legacy-rounding-characterization
evals.prompt: Before refactoring LegacyInvoiceCalculator, add a characterization test for the current pre-2025 tax rounding behavior. Nobody is sure if it is right, but old invoices must not change while we refactor.
evals.expected_output: Routes to legacy guidance, writes a characterization test that labels uncertainty, explains why behavior is pinned, and avoids presenting the current behavior as a permanent domain rule.

assertions.text: Loads or follows references/legacy-and-characterization.md
Includes rationale for preserving current legacy behavior during refactor
Does not treat unknown legacy behavior as a timeless product rule

evals.name: hard-to-test-payment-service
evals.prompt: I need tests for PaymentService. It constructs StripeClient internally, reads Date.now(), and sends receipts in the same method that calculates invoice totals. Please just mock whatever is needed.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the production code is hard to observe, recommends decomposing calculation, clock, gateway, and receipt boundaries before adding broad mocks, then suggests focused tests and adapter checks.

assertions.text: Loads or follows references/doubles-and-boundaries.md
Recommends improving production boundaries instead of only adding broad mocks
Does not expose private internals only for tests

evals.name: review-vague-mock-heavy-tests
evals.prompt: Review this diff: tests are named 'works' and 'handles error', most assertions are assertTrue/assertNotNull, and the order repository mock expects five internal calls. Is that okay?
evals.expected_output: Uses severity-first review, calls out misleading tests, weak assertions, and brittle implementation coupling, then suggests behavior names, observable assertions, and narrower doubles.

assertions.text: Loads or follows references/review-rubric.md
Prioritizes behavior gaps and brittleness before style nits
Identifies vague names and weak assertions as maintainability problems

evals.name: named-parameterized-edge-cases
evals.prompt: Convert these three copied validation tests into a parameterized test: empty email, malformed email, and email longer than 255 characters. Keep it readable for onboarding.
evals.expected_output: Creates a parameterized test with named cases that explain each boundary, keeps expected outcomes visible, and avoids an opaque anonymous data table.

assertions.text: Uses named dataset or case labels for each email boundary
Keeps the expected validation result visible
Does not hide all behavior in a generic helper

evals.name: review-false-positive-artifact-assertions
evals.prompt: Review evals/files/publish-config.spec.ts against this contract: production writes formatter.ts with `export default { mode: "strict" };`, writes formatter.ts.backup only when backup is true, and the backup must equal the old bytes. Identify tests that can pass while the contract is broken and show the smallest repair.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads side-effect guidance, catches the boolean-versus-content assertion and formatter.json.backup path drift, recommends reading the exact destination and backup bytes, and preserves the valid backup-content assertion.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/side-effects-and-compatibility.md
Identifies that existsSync returns a boolean and therefore cannot prove the previous file contents were replaced
Identifies formatter.json.backup as a different artifact from the production formatter.ts.backup path
Repairs the tests by asserting exact destination and backup contents, not only exit status or existence
Repairs the no-backup case by checking the actual formatter.ts.backup path is absent when backup is false
Does not discard the already exact backup-content assertion

evals.name: isolate-effects-across-supported-versions
evals.prompt: Our retry adapter supports SDK 2 through 4. SDK 4 adds an optional scheduleWithoutBlocking method. The current tests make a real HTTP call, call sleep(2), mutate a global SDK singleton, and run only on SDK 4. Redesign the focused tests and bounded CI coverage without hiding required failures behind broad skips.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to side-effect and compatibility guidance, denies unstubbed requests, fakes waiting while asserting meaningful backoff, restores global state, tests capability presence and absence, and includes the lowest supported plus current SDK combinations.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/side-effects-and-compatibility.md
Makes unstubbed network access fail and replaces real sleep with a controllable scheduler or clock
Restores the global SDK state so test order cannot affect the result
Tests capability-present and capability-absent paths plus the lowest and current supported SDK combinations
Uses a narrow capability reason for optional skips and fails with context when the requested behavior is required

evals.name: negative-disposable-port-check
evals.prompt: Give me a one-off shell command to test whether localhost port 8080 is open. I am not changing product code, do not want an automated test, and will discard the command immediately.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not trigger because the word test describes a disposable manual probe, not automated tests or durable test code.

assertions.text: Does not load maintainable-tests or produce fixture, mocking, coverage, isolation, or compatibility guidance
